Um, I don't think so? I mean, I'm not really sure if it's tied to being upset or angry. It's just kind of... always there. Like, I don't need to be mad to feel like I need to move.

I don't think I avoid anything because of it. I mean, I know I'm going to be fidgeting, but I still go. Like, I still go to the movies even though I'm shifting around in the seat the whole time.

Specific times? Um, no, I don't think so. It's not like it only happens in the morning or at night. It's just sort of... constant, I guess? 

Although, mornings are always so chaotic at our house anyway. Getting my daughter ready for school is like herding cats. I even bought those really expensive Brooks sneakers that they map to your arch type at the running store. The guy had me jog on a treadmill while he recorded my feet with an iPad. We had to park in this muddy field, and my husband's car got stuck. We had to pay a guy in a pickup truck fifty bucks to tow us out.

I actually thought about getting a fish tank for our living room, but I read online that saltwater tanks are a ton of work to keep the pH balanced and everything. I can barely keep my houseplants alive, let alone a bunch of tropical fish. I bought a fiddle leaf fig tree at the hardware store because they look so good in magazines, but all the leaves turned brown and fell off within a month. I think I overwatered it. Or maybe it didn't get enough light, since the big window in our living room faces north, so it's always kind of shadowy in there. \n\nBut um... no, I don't really skip out on activities just because I can't sit still. I just kind of power through it, you know?\n\nDoctor: Do you notice that your restlessness tends to happen at specific times of the day?\n\nPatient: Specific times? Um, no, I don't think so. Um, overwhelmed? Yeah, I guess so. Actually, that's kind of what brings me in... I just feel like I can’t settle in my own body anymore, you know? Especially when I have to sit down and do something quiet, like filling out paperwork or going over the household budget with my husband. 

We use this app for our budget, but I honestly hate it because the categories never make sense. Like, where are you supposed to put the money you spend on birthday gifts? Does that go under 'entertainment' or 'miscellaneous'? Last month I bought my niece this adorable little dollhouse for her fifth birthday. It was made of real wood, not that cheap plastic stuff, and it had all these tiny little furniture pieces. The couch even had real fabric on it. My sister said it took her three hours to put it together because the instructions were just pictures with no words. I hate when companies do that. It's like building IKEA furniture. We bought a dresser from IKEA once for the guest room, and it sat in boxes on the floor for a solid month before we finally tackled it. And then we realized we put the drawer tracks on backward. The guest room is mostly just storage right now anyway. I really want to paint it a nice sage green, but picking out paint colors is so stressful. You bring home those little paper swatches, and they look completely different on the wall than they do in the store under those fluorescent lights. 

But yeah, when I'm trying to focus on stuff like that, the paperwork or the planning, the restless feeling is just... it's really bad. I just can't settle down.

Before I was seven? Yeah, definitely. Looking back, this was already just... part of who I was in elementary school. I was always the girl with the completely messy desk. And then we realized we put the drawer tracks on backward. The guest room is mostly just storage right now anyway. I really want to paint it a nice sage green, but picking out paint colors is so stressful. I'm not really worrying about anything when I can't sit still, I just physically have to keep moving.\n\nDoctor: Is your restlessness something that you experience all the time, or are there times when it goes away completely?\n\nPatient: Um, goes away completely? I don't really think it ever completely stops. Even when I'm just at home for the day, I'm always doing something. He used to have this old Ford pickup truck that he kept running for like twenty years just by tinkering with it on the weekends. It was this awful mustard yellow color, but he loved it. People always have these big plans for projects and then they just never follow through, you know? Like my husband's plan to build a deck in the backyard.
